§aLoaded Chunks: ON
§6Loaded Chunk Mode (Restart Required)
§aAfter restarting with it off: no chunk-scan events, tick handler, processing queue, or chunk-state tracking are registered; runtime cost is effectively the same as not having this feature.
§eAfter restarting with it on: existing chunks are queued for one-time processing when they load, using the current replacement rules.
§ePerformance while enabled: medium to high during processing; at most 1 chunk is processed per tick to avoid burst scanning.
§cMore old loaded chunks and taller worlds take longer; completed chunks are marked and are not rescanned for the same rule type.
§aSave the current block merge rules. The Loaded Chunks switch only changes the next-launch state and takes effect after a full game restart.
§cChanging this switch requires a full game restart. Saving it only changes the next-launch state; it does not enable or disable the system live.

gui.realmcontrol.structure.biomes.hint: Left click includes, right click excludes, click again to clear
tooltip.realmcontrol.structure_controlle: Container / spawner mode: right-click opens its marker, Shift + right-click adds it to a batch; entity mode: right-click keeps or leaves it out
msg.realmcontrol.structure.marker.entity: This entity is not in the scan (it moved or appeared since); scan again
msg.realmcontrol.structure.marker.no_pro: This is not inside any structure draft
msg.realmcontrol.structure.marker.no_ent: No entity in sight within %s blocks
msg.realmcontrol.structure.marker.batch: %s gathered; right-click one to open the markers
msg.realmcontrol.structure.marker.no_con: This is not a scanned container
msg.realmcontrol.structure.marker.no_spa: This is not a scanned spawner
msg.realmcontrol.structure.publish.unkno: These loot tables do not exist, nothing was published: %s
msg.realmcontrol.structure.publish.done_: Published %s (%s biomes) to this world's datapacks folder; it generates in new chunks after re-entering the world
msg.realmcontrol.structure.loot.bad_id: Not a valid loot table id: %s
msg.realmcontrol.structure.loot.exists: Loot table %s already exists; choose another id
msg.realmcontrol.structure.loot.no_sourc: No loot table file to copy: %s
msg.realmcontrol.structure.loot.created: Created loot table %s (KineticCore data pack realmcontrol)
gui.realmcontrol.structure.action.marker: Loot tables of containers, mobs of spawners, entities kept or left out
gui.realmcontrol.structure.markers.title: Markers
gui.realmcontrol.structure.markers.searc: Search blocks, entities or loot tables…
gui.realmcontrol.structure.markers.empty: This draft has no containers, spawners or entities
gui.realmcontrol.structure.markers.selec: Select a marker on the left
gui.realmcontrol.structure.markers.unsav: The marker changes are not saved. Discard them?
gui.realmcontrol.structure.markers.conta: The container holds the scanned items
The container is empty until a player first opens it; then the loot table fills it
gui.realmcontrol.structure.markers.table: Pick one of the server's loot tables
Create a table in the KineticCore data pack: empty, a copy, or made from the container's items
Opens it in ContentStudio's loot editor; Back returns here
Loot table %s does not exist; publishing is refused
%s entries name missing items and are left out when it loads: %s
gui.realmcontrol.structure.markers.conta: Vanilla cannot fill this kind of container from a loot table; it keeps its items
Every placement rolls its own loot: vanilla gives each container a new random seed when it places a structure. Select several containers to change them together.
gui.realmcontrol.structure.markers.spawn: Choose the mobs and weights, delays, counts and ranges
Delay %s–%s ticks · %s per spawn · up to %s nearby · player within %s · range %s
No mobs chosen yet; it is published as scanned
Custom spawners are written with vanilla's fields: mobs are picked by weight, delays are in ticks (20 ticks = 1 second).
gui.realmcontrol.structure.markers.entit: Whether this type is kept or left out; change single ones below
Left-click switches kept / left out, right-click follows the type again
gui.realmcontrol.structure.loot.new.id.t: Lower-case letters, digits and _ - . /, e.g. realmcontrol:chests/siheyuan/main
gui.realmcontrol.structure.loot.new.kind: One equal-weight entry per kind of item, with the counts and data of the scanned items
One pool without entries, to fill in ContentStudio
Starts from another table's content; that table stays as it is
gui.realmcontrol.structure.loot.new.help: The table goes into the %s folder of the KineticCore data pack realmcontrol, and the selected containers use it. It loads when the world is entered again; with ContentStudio its file can be edited directly. If a mod whose items it names is removed, only those entries are left out.
gui.realmcontrol.structure.spawner.title: Spawner
Spawners · %s
gui.realmcontrol.structure.spawner.choos: Tick the mobs to spawn in the entity selector; new ones get weight 1
gui.realmcontrol.structure.spawner.weigh: How likely the current mob is picked, relative to the others
gui.realmcontrol.structure.spawner.empty: No mobs yet; use Choose mobs…
gui.realmcontrol.structure.spawner.max_n: Pauses while this many are around; vanilla 6
gui.realmcontrol.structure.spawner.playe: Works only with a player this close; vanilla 16
gui.realmcontrol.structure.spawner.spawn: How far around it mobs appear; vanilla 4
gui.realmcontrol.structure.spawner.help: Apply sets every spawner selected on the markers page to these values.
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.title: Save Options
Saves these options and writes the data pack with them
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.block_en: Off writes blocks only: empty containers, blank signs
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.loot.too: Off keeps the scanned items in every container
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.spawners: Off keeps every spawner as scanned
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.entities: Off writes no entities; on keeps or leaves them out as marked
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.persiste: Like the mobs of vanilla structures, they stay when players are far away
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.clean_en: Removes tamed owners, leashes, villager gossip and remembered places; UUIDs are already gone after the scan
Off writes the blocks inside the cut-outs too
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.target.k: config/kineticcore/datapack/data/realmcontrol: ships with the mod pack, every world gets it
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.target.w: Where vanilla keeps data packs: only this world, for maps and servers
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.target.z: Written to kineticcore/structure_exports and not loaded, to use elsewhere
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.both_for: Writes structures / structure and loot_tables / loot_table, so one pack loads in both versions
Only 1.20.1 can: older versions cannot read structures saved by newer ones
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.summary: Containers: %s with loot tables, %s keep items · spawners: %s custom, %s as scanned · entities: %s kept, %s left out
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.unknown_: Loot tables that do not exist; publishing is refused: %s
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.partial_: These tables name missing items, left out when they load: %s
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.help: Save keeps the options in the draft; Publish writes the data pack. Structure data packs load when the world is entered again (restart a server), and only new chunks get them.
msg.realmcontrol.structure.publish.no_ji: Tile %s has no cell for its jigsaw block (every cell holds a block entity or a mod's block)
msg.realmcontrol.structure.generation.sy: Wrote the generation rules of %s into its published files (%s biomes); they apply once the world is entered again (restart a server)
gui.realmcontrol.structure.generation.en: Switched off, the structure set is written with a chance of 0 and nothing generates; applies once the world is entered again after saving
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.tier.sma: Small: published as one vanilla jigsaw piece
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.tier.med: Medium: cut into %s×%s tiles (%s×%s blocks each) that vanilla jigsaw puts back together; the templates take about %s MB once loaded (kept until the world is left)
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.tier.meg: Mega: cut into %s×%s tiles (%s×%s blocks each) that RealmControl places chunk by chunk where vanilla's site picking puts it; RealmControl must be installed, and at most 64 tiles are loaded at a time
msg.realmcontrol.structure.publish.mega_: Mega structures can only be published to the KineticCore data pack: they need RealmControl to generate, and without it KineticCore leaves them out so the world still loads
A mega structure needs a separation of at least %s chunks (its footprint is %s blocks), or two of them overlap
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.mega_tar: Mega structures can only be published to the KineticCore data pack
gui.realmcontrol.structure.generation.fo: Fills below the building down to the ground (64 blocks at most) and clears the terrain above it up to the surface; cut-outs stay natural
Fills below the building down to the ground (64 blocks at most); the terrain above stays
Placed as it is: it may hang over gaps or be buried under terrain
Block id the foundation is filled with, for example minecraft:stone
gui.realmcontrol.structure.generation.su: Kept out: other structures do not start inside its footprint (and 64 blocks around it), and lakes and forest boulders do not cut into it
gui.realmcontrol.structure.generation.me: Mega structure: a separation of at least %s chunks keeps two of them from overlapping
gui.realmcontrol.worldgen.preview.mega_n: This mega structure has no draft to preview (its preview reads the structure editor's draft)
gui.realmcontrol.structure.action.test.t: Places a copy where you stand to see it as it generates; the covered area is saved first, so it can be undone. Up to %s×%s (medium and small) only
gui.realmcontrol.structure.test.title: Test Placement
gui.realmcontrol.structure.test.message: Places “%s” (%s×%s×%s, set %s blocks into the ground) centred where you stand, with loot tables, spawners and entities as the save options write them. The covered area is saved first, so it can be undone.
gui.realmcontrol.structure.test.undo.mes: Puts the area of the test placement of “%s” (from %s, %s, %s) back as it was, and removes the entities it placed.
gui.realmcontrol.structure.test.other.me: This world already has a test placement of “%s” (from %s, %s, %s); there can be one at a time. Undo it first?
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.rejoin.t: Publishes, then saves and enters this world again so the structure takes effect (not for a ZIP export)
gui.realmcontrol.structure.save.rejoin.u: Single-player worlds only (not while open to LAN); on a server, publish and restart it
msg.realmcontrol.structure.test.busy: A test placement or undo is running; wait for it to finish
msg.realmcontrol.structure.test.mega: Mega structures cannot be test placed; up to %s×%s only
msg.realmcontrol.structure.test.exists: There is a test placement of “%s”; undo it first
msg.realmcontrol.structure.test.height: It does not fit: Y=%s to Y=%s is outside the world's height; try another height
msg.realmcontrol.structure.test.source: The test placement would cover the place the draft was scanned from; go somewhere else
msg.realmcontrol.structure.test.cancelle: Test placement cancelled; the world is unchanged
msg.realmcontrol.structure.test.stopped: Test placement stopped; what was placed can be undone
msg.realmcontrol.structure.test.undo_sto: Undo stopped; undo again to finish
msg.realmcontrol.structure.test.none: There is no test placement to undo
msg.realmcontrol.structure.test.undone: Undid the test placement of “%s” and removed %s entities
